Our research indicates that the proportion of superfluous connections that can be removed is substantial, with results ranging from 30% to 99%, depending on the network type. Notably, we observed similar pruning capabilities across various types of networks, including those using convolutional and fully connected architectures. To further validate the robustness of our findings, we examined the impact of data augmentation and found that pruning rates are relatively insensitive to variations in amount and type of available data. Moreover, we explored the applicability of our approach to noise reduction and observed comparable results for both Gaussian noise and randomly flipped labels. Our results suggest that pruning dense connections can lead to a substantial reduction in network complexity without compromising performance. This discovery raises the possibility of unearthing previously underutilized structural insights in existing neural networks, and could potentially accelerate the development of more efficient networks.

In recent years, "Sudden Wealth!" has gained popularity in Mexico as a way to potentially transform one's life through a lottery-style investment called "doble aposte," which offers the possibility of doubling payouts. Focusing on the possibility of achieving life-changing financial gains, we develop a quantitative model grounded in an investor's goal of accumulating wealth over their lifetime. By assuming the investor aims to reach a high threshold of wealth to significantly enhance their expected wealth by the time of retirement, and by applying the Heavy Tails Theory to their future wealth distribution, our model demonstrates that the most effective strategy to achieve this goal is to adopt a high-risk tolerance for non-lottery investments and then allocate a portion of their wealth to "Sudden Wealth!" through the "doble aposte." We find that the optimal strategy for participating in this lottery depends on the level of risk an investor is willing to take, with moderate to extremely high risk-tolerant investors increasing their lottery investments as their wealth increases. We further show that supporting responsible promotion strategies in the lottery industry can benefit both the "Sudden Wealth!" industry and the national economy by reducing the likelihood of young investors making irrational investment decisions and minimizing the risk of bankruptcy and unemployment in the national economy.

The large-charge expansion technique, specifically the $\phi^Q$ operator method, has recently been shown to enable precise determination of the spectrum in the $O(N)$-symmetric theory. This approach involves expanding in large charge $Q$ and combining it with the known $Q\to\infty$ limit to extract values at finite $Q$. Recent work has demonstrated how to extract values at finite $Q$ in a systematic manner, beginning with the large $N$ limit and then using a combination of techniques to extract values at finite $N$. A key component of this method is the six-loop anomalous dimension of the $\phi^Q\bar\phi^Q$ operator, which we have now computed. This involves determining a specific set of integrals in perturbation theory, specifically the six-loop sector, to obtain the desired result. This information contributes to the precise determination of the $SU(2)$ minimal models' spectrum, for large but fixed $Q$.

Our research introduces electron-phonon coupling mechanisms involving electron and phonon interactions with specific crystal lattice orientations, namely in-plane and out-of-plane plane. We demonstrate that electron-phonon coupling mechanisms novel mechanisms can significantly influence the behavior of valley electrons in two-dimensional materials, leading to a disruption of valley degrees of freedom and introducing new electron-phonon coupling mechanisms. These new mechanisms can be controlled by external fields, opening up new avenues in valley electronics and allowing for the creation of valley polarons with a decrease in mass, thereby enhancing valley electronics performance.

The VisDA 2022 Challenge seeks unsupervised domain adaptation for visual tasks, using seen datasets to create models capable of handling unseen tasks in un familiar domain settings. We will address the Challenging 2022 subset, characterized by significant domain shifts, intense local competition, and substantial domain shift. Our solution combines several well-known methods to tackle Challenging 2022. Specifically, we submit four strategies: 1) utilizing the source dataset to train a model, 2) applying a self-supervised learning approach, 3) integrating our self-supervised model with a domain adaptation technique, and 4) using a generative model to handle the domain shift. The first approach is our baseline model, the second leverages self-supervised learning to improve model generalization, the third combines our self-supervised method with a technique that aligns the source and target domains, and the fourth uses a generative model to translate the source domain to the target domain. The fusion of these models yields superior performance when combining the top-performing models on specific tasks.

t-SNE is a widely employed method for reducing high-dimensional data to lower-dimensional representations, particularly in data visualization. Its underlying assumption however, involves an Euclidean distance-based affinity measure in both reduced and original dimensional spaces. Due to the local-to-global distance scaling property, using a spherical distance-based measure could be advantageous for spherical data. We propose a novel t-SNE algorithm, VMF-SNE, which utilizes the von Mises-Fisher distribution to model the affinity of data points in both reduced 2D and original D dimensional spaces. We evaluate the performance of VMF-SNE on both 2D visualization and local-reconstruction tasks using MNIST, CIFAR10, and 3D volumetric data. We find that VMF-SNE preserves more spherical characteristics and yields higher fidelity local data reconstructions.

Diagrammatic Monte Carlo methods are used to investigate the properties of the two-dimensional Fermi polaron beyond what perturbative methods can achieve. By employing an alternative strategy where the model's exact strong-coupling result (the no-pair limit) and the exact weak-coupling result (the fourth-order Padé approximation) serve as boundary conditions, our approach significantly enhances the accuracy of Diagrammatic Monte Carlo methods across the entire coupling strength spectrum. The results show that this optimized method accurately predicts the polaron's energy and the effective mass near both the weak-coupling and strong-coupling limits. Furthermore, this method reveals the presence of a stable bound state under boson-fermion interactions at low densities, even in the case of two bosons.

In this hybrid digital-analog approach to fermionic systems, a simplified dynamic similar to the natural Hamiltonian, as found in the fermionic quantum-atom interaction model, is created through the use of a digital algorithm. This artificial dynamic serves as a precise approximation of the target dynamic, achieved by carefully selecting a sequence of non-unitary operations. These operations, applied in conjunction with a single non-classical pulse, significantly reduce the circuit complexity for simulating time-evolution. Our experimental results, conducted using a hybrid digital-analog quantum computer, showcase the advantages of this simplified approach over its purely digital counterpart.

Graph polynomials have been employed for over three decades to study vertices, edges, and various graph substructures. Evaluating these polynomials yields the chromatic polynomial and polynomial interpretations of chromatic indices. Each such polynomial polynomial polynomial generates a sequence based on its coefficients or values, and it is proposed that these sequences share key characteristics such as log-concavity, unimodality, and gap properties. To substantiate this, researchers found a polynomial polynomial polynomial giving a sequence that is strictly log-concave and unimodal in certain contexts, such as when evaluating bipartite cycles. Further investigation reveals the discovery of non-unimodal and weakly log-concave examples among these polynomials, suggesting the need for novel methods in proving unimodality through more refined tools.

We derive an expression for the Hitchin connection associated with a genus-two Lattes map, a key element in computationally determining modular forms for a family of curves known as Lattes curves, an approach first proposed by M. Duffin et al. as part of their Quantum Riemann Surface Project. Focus is given to the Lattes map family's subset, specifically those with a minimal Veech ratio. Leveraging D. Guo's and Faber's earlier findings on the genus-two lambda dispersion relation, we compute the large-order asymptotic expansion of a modular form family relevant to this computation and employ it to describe the large-n behavior of a determinant of Laplacians on a genus-two Lattes manifold. In doing so, we also determine the holomorphic anomaly equations solutions in this case, comparing our findings against a case study previously examined by Duffin et al. in their Quantum Riemann Surface Project.

This paper explores the effectiveness of scrum projects during remote work. Previous studies suggest that scrum teams might encounter challenges adapting to remote work. We conducted a comprehensive investigation into how remote work impacts the performance of scrum projects. Using a mixed-methods approach, we analyzed data from 10 scrum projects over the past three years to determine the influence of remote work on project success. Our findings indicate that: (1) scrum projects can be successful even when teams work remotely, (3) there is no link between remote work and reduced effectiveness in scrum projects, (4) remote work and scrum are compatible but remote work may create challenges for scrum teams.

The Gau-Wu number represents the minimum number of non-zero entries required in the difference matrix between two Hermitian positive semidefinite matrices, entry-wise. This study delves into specific matrix types to determine the Gau-Wu number, utilizing more general results applicable theorems as a foundation. Ultimately, this work classifies the Gau-Ww number for all $4 \times 4$ matrices and selects certain arrowhead matrices as well, aiming to provide insights and future avenues of research.

In a high-energy collision of lead nuclei at 5.02 TeV, an experiment at the Large Hadron Collider measured the elliptic flow of electrons originating from mesons containing beauty particles. The elliptic flow was analyzed within specific ranges of transverse momentum, particularly between 2 and 100 GeV/c, and at varying transverse impact parameters, encompassing all degrees of ellipticity. The findings were compared to theoretical models incorporating the contributions of heavy quarks and gluons, as well as models that consider only heavy quarks, and also to theoretical calculations and experimental observations of differential cross-sections for beauty-hadrons in proton-proton collisions at 7 TeV.

In topological data analysis, the method called persistent homology is utilized to measure the robustness of topological properties in input data sets. A new approach, the chromatic alpha complex, has been developed to analyze graphs by converting them into simplicial complexes. By applying topological data analysis techniques to these complexes, the method offers an efficient colorability test, while also enabling various other analysis tests. Our study focuses on investigating how the persistence in chromatic alpha complexes is connected to the number of colors required to effectively color a given graph.

This work investigates the difference in General Degree of Freedom (GDoF) between Binary Power Control and Optimal Power Control in a environment where multiple transmitters and receivers coexist and some of them interfere with each other while having knowledge of the channel connections. Our analysis, which builds on a previous study that only considered two transmitters and receivers, reveals that the gain of Optimal Power Control over Binary Power Control is proportional to the square root of the number of transmitters and receivers when the number of transmitters and receivers is large. To arrive at this conclusion, we derived a new set of inequalities that determine the maximum possible GDoF and then created a scenario where the inequalities closely match each other. Our analysis also shows that the inequalities play a significant role in constraining the achievable GDoF and that the exact solution lies somewhere within a region bounded by the individual contributions of each transmitters and receivers. Our study provides a valuable insight into the limitations and potential of different power control strategies in a environment where multiple transmitters and receivers coexist and will be a useful tool for further analysis of multi-transmitter and multi-receiver interference networks.

Auditing processes often involve categorization, yet pre-defined classifications can be inflexible and mislead when dealing with uncertain or diverse data. To address this, we propose a novel approach combining formal concept analysis and Dempster-Shafer theory, which utilizes vague contextual elements expressed as mass functions to establish categorizations directly from auditing data sets, uncovering inherent structures. This methodology demonstrates its worth through experimental evaluations on real-world auditing data, highlighting its efficiency in insightful categorization.

The Strauss process, which is a point process, has numerous applications in real-world phenomena. By adjusting the parameter $\rho$ of a Strauss process, it can mimic the behavior of a Poisson point process, showcasing varying degrees of point clustering. By linking the $\rho$ values of multiple Strauss processes, we can model complex point process patterns, especially when $\rho$ is time-dependent. Our proposed "stitching" method provides a versatile approach for generating point process samples, which can be used to obtain alternative statistical tests for point process data. The effectiveness of this approach is shown in simulations, where it outperforms traditional methods in detecting space-time point process patterns, especially when there is heterogeneity present.

In the context of quantum theory, the generalized uncertainty principle serves as a fundamental constraint, preventing the transformation to arbitrarily small length or momentum spaces. This paper explores how the GUP modifies the transformations between Galilean and Lorentz frames. Our analysis reveals that the GUP leads to observable length discrepancies between inertial frames in GALTON spaces. Additionally, we investigate how the GUP impacts the movement of a particle within such a space.

Multitasking scheduling in service industries is expanding due to companies' desire to employ workers full-time and enhance their flexibility in adapting to varying customer demands. We explore a complex optimization issue where a service provider aims to schedule multiple tasks completed by a shared worker using a dynamic, real-time algorithm. The tasks complete instantly if the worker is available, and we assume the tasks are randomly timed and occur at a rate that can change. Our research involves designing a deterministic, online algorithm to determine when the shared worker should be idle. We compare the algorithm's performance to the ideal optimal schedule in terms of the total time spent being idle. We establish a lower limit on performance improvement and develop a algorithm that comes close to this limit under most real-world conditions. We also investigate how changes in task arrival rates affect the algorithm's performance and provide theoretical and practical evidence to show that an equal distribution of tasks affects performance optimally.

A cutting-edge technique for enhancing legged robots' locomotion capabilities on various types of terrain is the introduction of compliant feet. Introducing compliance in a robot's contact point allows it to effectively manage and adapt to uneven and soft terrain conditions. In this paper, a model is developed that simulates the dynamic behavior of a monopod robot hopping on soft terrain with a compliant foot. A multi-objective optimization approach is implemented to enhance the monopod's jumping performance and adapt its controller specifically for soft terrain conditions. Through simulation testing and comparison with a rigid-foot monopod, results demonstrate that the compliant-foot optimization significantly boosts the monopod's vertical distance traveled by approximately 10.8% on soft terrain.

In the rapidly expanding Internet of Things (IoT) ecosystem, ensuring secure and reliable services is of utmost importance. Ensuring smooth connectivity and enabling seamless service updates are critical aspects of maintaining high customer satisfaction. However, due to the limited resources possessed by IoT devices, these tasks become even more challenging. In this study, the authors evaluate the performance of firmware updates in the largest IoT network in the world, utilizing a variety of evaluation criteria such as power consumption, network activity, data transfer duration, and success rates. A key finding reveals that mesh routing significantly impacts firmware update processes, prompting the development of a new strategy based on link quality assessment to minimize protocol overhead and optimize power consumption. This novel method has demonstrated substantial improvements over existing approaches, resulting in a notable reduction in power consumption (up to 35%) and data transfer (up to 26%). A comprehensive discussion on security concerns is also presented to address the challenges associated with IoT updates.

We've studied the transition many-body localization (MBL) using the density of states (DOS) and eigenstate texture. Our research focused on a specific metric called the participation ratio of large-scale wave functions, referred to as the r-body participation ratio ($Pr(r)$). By analyzing the probability distribution of $Pr(r)$, we discovered a universal feature that distinguishes the MBL and delocalized phases. This characteristic behavior is marked by the scaling of the second moment with the system size, with a specific exponent of 3/2 being significant for distinguishing the two phases. Our results also show that this measure is highly effective in identifying the phase transition and the associated critical point. Furthermore, we have demonstrated that this metric is capable of capturing the complex nature of the phase transition and the associated critical behavior.

To make the most out of human expertise, interactive machine learning is employed, where a machine learning agent seeks an optimal solution from a given solution space by asking binary questions and drawing on human knowledge. Current research has mostly focused on finding a single best solution within a pre-defined range, but often people can provide multiple solutions and may not be able to pinpoint a singular ideal solution. We address this limitation by proposing a novel interactive method that accommodates a given number of targets and operates within a fixed budget. This method learns to represent the search space based on the problem's constraints and then uses this understanding to decide which question to ask humans to get the most informative response. The empirical results demonstrate that our method substantially outperforms existing techniques in efficiency and solution quality when handling multiple targets.

Machine and quantum learning algorithms are particularly susceptible to adversarial threats, which can compromise their security. This study investigates a type of threat known as 'universal adversarial examples' that remains effective even if the attacker lacks access to the target classifier. A previously introduced method, 'universal transfer attack,' is applied and modified to mount these threats, and we show that the threat can not only target a single quantum classifier but multiple quantum classifiers as well, and even within the same variational quantum eigensolver approach used to solve specific tasks. Our approach can create 'adversarial perturbations' that are effective even for a quantum classifier operating in a different field, and it can circumvent countermeasures such as 'random rotation defense.' While we focus on certain quantum algorithms, the threat is not limited to a specific quantum classifier, and it can pose a significant threat to the future of quantum machine learning.

We examine Steklov eigenvalues in nearly spherical domains of three dimensions.  Building on our earlier research, which demonstrated the eigenvalues' analytic dependence on initial parameters, we further analyze the impact of an additional parameter, the amplitude function's $H^1(\mathbb{S}^2)$-norm, by identifying a specific threshold, $\delta_0$.  For amplitude functions within this threshold, we establish that the first $N$ Steklov eigenvalues converge to zero at a rate of $O(\varepsilon \log(1/\varepsilon))$ and the remaining $N$th through $\varepsilon$th eigenvalues diverge to infinity.  This result is derived from a refined lower bound for the sum of the first $N$ eigenvalues, established by utilizing a specially designed test function within Heintze-Kapovich-Yau variational spaces.  In contrast, for amplitude functions exceeding the threshold, we show the existence of eigenvalues with values of order $O(\varepsilon)$.

Conformance checking focuses on comparing modeled process behavior to observed process behavior from logs, a task known as conformance checking. Most existing approaches in conformance checking deal with complete process traces recorded in an event log. However, there have been instances where process behavior in an event log isn't fully captured due to a technique called black boxing, a process where a developer intentionally hides process details in an application. A developer may do this by integrating off-the-shelf components, using a single function call to represent multiple actions, or incorporating a service's API in a business process, thus replacing multiple actions with a single action. To address this limitation, we present new techniques - infix and postfix alignments - aimed at analyzing black-boxed event logs against process models. We established that postfix alignments provide greater flexibility than infix alignments, allowing for a better fit between a black-boxed event log and its process model. We demonstrated the capabilities of postfix alignments with a real-world example where we applied a product recommendation engine to an insurance company and replaced multiple actions with a single action, thus black-boxing the process. We analyzed black-boxed event logs of users purchasing insurance policies, comparing them to a process model of users purchasing those policies. We used postfix alignments to identify gaps between a black-boxed event log and its process model that were beyond the capabilities of an infix alignments approach.

Accurate prediction of radio signal strength is essential for designing and optimizing cellular networks, as it enables engineers to strategically place and tune base stations, covering desired areas while minimizing costs. Traditional methods for modeling signal strength, such as empirical and deterministic approaches, each have significant drawbacks. Empirical methods rely on site-specific calibration and local environmental factors, as well as the known near-field effect. Deterministic methods, relying on line-of-sight blockage and geographical data, often fail to capture urban and indoor environments. In an attempt to overcome these limitations, machine learning and deep learning models have been developed, leveraging data-driven simulations to create more accurate signaling models. A novel approach presented in this paper utilizes deep convolutional neural networks to predict cellular network signal strength, leveraging the spatial distribution of digital terrain maps and base station transmission data. Our model achieves high accuracy on simulated and real-world urban environments and can also make test data-Driven predictions without requiring line-of-sight information.

A straightforward semantics is proposed for temporal planning. We define and formally establish the logic within the interactive theorem prover Isabelle/HOL, and then obtain a validation algorithm based on that semantics. By using a formal Isabelle/HOL proof, it is shown that the validation algorithm faithfully represents the developed semantics. We also demonstrate through practical experiments that the verification of the algorithm is efficient.

Power system expansion planning models, used to integrate renewable energy and reduce emissions, are susceptible to varying power system characteristics due to their reliance on parametric assumptions. This research introduces sensitivity analysis for DC OPF models, revealing the influence of key parameters such as transmission capacity, power flow limits, and line resistance on energy production, transmission capabilities, and power system investment costs. The study finds that models incorporating sensitive parameters like transmission capacity and line resistance yield more realistic and cost-effective results, especially under high levels of renewable energy integration. Moreover, incorporating sensitive parameters significantly enhances the model's ability to model grid expansion activities, enabling cost savings of up to 10% compared to models ignoring these parameters.

This study establishes the global existence of classical solutions for the Vlasov-Poisson and the ionic Vlasov-Poisson models within confined areas, under specified boundary conditions that include a particular reflection scenario for the Vlasov equation.

When developers encounter issues with their software, they initiate searches by inputting specific term(s) and these are usually derived from their bug or error messages, which can include the scope of bugs or errors. Research shows that effective search term selection impacts location suggestion quality. Therefore, this study proposes a method, Information Retrieval based Search Term Identification for Concept Location (STRICT), to enhance the quality of generated search terms based on developer input and subsequently improve search and retrieval outcomes. Data from two large open-source projects, Android and IntelliJ-IDEA, along with issue tracking systems from Redmine and Jira, were used to train and evaluate the STRICT approach. The results demonstrate that, as the size of issues grows, so does the effectiveness of search terms developed using the STRICT approach. Furthermore, this study successfully integrated the STRICT approach into Redmine and validated its benefits.

Researchers have discovered a method to control the flow and stiffness of a highly viscous gel using sound waves. Ultrasonic vibrations applied to a thixotropic colloidal gel cause a significant increase in its viscosity, resulting in the creation of a highly elastic, solid-like material. This sound-induced solidification process enables the gel to withstand mechanical stress without deforming. Moreover, when ultrasonic vibrations are present, the gel's stiffness and tensile strength are significantly enhanced, allowing it to resist its own weight and break under external force. When the vibrations are turned off, the gel returns to its original soft state. This innovative phenomenon is known as rheo-acoustics and has the potential to transform the properties of gels in response to external stimuli.
This research paper delves into the analysis of the Collatz conjecture's behavior, focusing on its underlying dynamics and behavior patterns.

To enhance transparency and trust in machine learning models' performance,
especially in critical areas like education, we propose integrating an auxiliary
explanation mechanism using mathematical equations from academic sources. This
form of explanation can effectively illustrate the connections between various
concepts, such as "Pythagoras' theorem" between "squares" and "right triangles".
We investigate the feasibility of using mathematical entity linking to provide
explanations for ML models, particularly in the context of categorizing academic
publications based on topics. Our experiments, conducted with the TMC dataset
comprising 777 STEM publications and 7 specific math topics, demonstrate that
mathematical entity linking can accurately identify and associate mathematical
concepts within the texts, achieving a performance comparable to existing
entity linking models. Additionally, we find that an ensemble approach of multiple
mathematical entity linking models leads to improved classification performance,
outperforming baseline models with average improvements of 2.1% and a maximum
gain of 4.3% in classification accuracy.

To achieve stable pairings, the Deferred Acceptance algorithm takes time proportional to the square of the number of agents, but it's not necessary for stability in every case. A modification called FastDA completes the process in linear time when the input data is randomly ordered. FastDA has the flexibility to choose between these two approaches by adjusting how many proposals an agent can make at a time. Research shows that there's a limit to the efficiency of intermediate approaches and reveals that FastDA's limit lies somewhere in between linear and superlinear time.

Current evaluation metrics for summarization models have limitations in
assessing the quality of generated summaries. Perplexity-based metrics are
insensitive to word-order variations, while classification methods lack the
nuance to evaluate the diversity of summaries. To address these shortcomings,
we propose a new evaluation metric called SummScore, which leverages a
Transformer-based cross-encoder to compare the generated summary with the
original text, thereby capturing the level of compression and fidelity to the
original meaning. To improve evaluation reliability, a model is fine-tuned on a
high-quality dataset and further enhanced with ensemble techniques. Our
evaluation using benchmark datasets and human annotations confirms that
SummScore outperforms existing evaluation metrics and closely aligns with human
assessment. The summscore.py package can be found on GitHub at
https://github.com/jianchang1999/summscore.

A new method for extracting a sparse signal from cross-related data is presented. This type of measurement is formulated as the inner product between the signal and a signal from the same high-dimensional, sparse set, but is not limited to this class. This signal measurement is referred to as being based on quadratic forms for convenience. Although the cross-correlation properties make the problem inherently linked to the Cholesky decomposition, the general case does not necessarily adhere to this specific application, so the term quadratic measurements is used broadly. A particular measurement matrix in this context involves computing whether two signals overlap at a given shift. This signal recovery problem can be reformulated as an optimization problem in the time domain for certain problems such as deconvolution. This reformulation, performed over a hypercube with a convex objective function derived from the cross-correlation matrix, is proven to converge to a globally optimal solution under a given sparsity constraint from correlated bases. This signal measurement type can be used practically, among other things, to perform deconvolution operations. Additionally, an efficient algorithm based on the subgradient method is proposed for solving this optimization problem, along with convergence proofs and the development of subgradient methods. This subgradient method is further enhanced by a fast, iterative, and greedy approach, which is particularly effective when dealing with large-scale problems. This method, called Fast Signal Recovery (FRES), is demonstrated to perform on par with or even outperform state-of-the-art methods for sparse signal extraction through simulation results.

The conventional approach to 3D object detection, where camera and LiDAR data are combined, is no longer tenable due to its vulnerability to LiDAR malfunctions under adverse weather conditions. New approaches, which prioritize data alignment and fusion within a unified framework, aim to resolve these limitations. Nevertheless, as this field is still in its nascent stages, these methods often compromise on model simplicity and robustness. Our proposed method, BEVFusion, addresses these challenges by incorporating an efficient fusion module into a standard framework, thereby significantly reducing computational overhead and model complexity. Our experiments demonstrate that BEVFusion enhances robustness against weather-related LiDAR impairments, while also outperforming a wide array of state-of-the-art models with the simplest possible architecture. Furthermore, the open-sourcing of our code and models will facilitate future advancements in this area.

We have studied numerical simulations of incompressible fluid turbulence, focusing on a specific range of scales. We've represented random forces as combinations of Bessel functions and found that the scale dependence of the resulting velocity and energy spectra depends on the force spectrum. We found that only certain models of random forces are capable of producing a well-defined inertial range with a stable equilibrium, a property that is essential for generating the dissipation-range of fluid turbulence. Furthermore, we found that a specific random force model is capable of replicating the energy cascade of a real turbulent flow when combined with numerical simulations.

Recent experiments observing diffraction patterns within a liquid, induced by a laser and a grating, have shown that the pattern formation is self-induced and not uniform. The formation is linked to the liquid's dynamically shifting properties resulting from the laser heating. An equation proposed in 1972 by Muller describes the liquid profile's evolution but the accuracy of this model, and the liquid parameters, remain unclear, hindering the understanding of the phenomenon and limiting the development of novel methods for controlling liquid properties. Our study presents the first comprehensive and self-contained numerical simulation of the experiment. By comparing simulated and measured diffraction patterns, we confirm the validity of the 1972 model and establish precise values for the liquid parameters.

Discussions among designers hold significant potential for enhancing the collective problem-solving capabilities of a development team.  Effective extraction of valuable insights from designer conversations requires an understanding of the discussions' context and content.  However, existing content-based mining methods are plagued by language inconsistencies, structural discrepancies, and NLP algorithm variations that hinder comparison and render results difficult to replicate and trustworthiness questionable.  

This study introduces a novel framework for evaluating the stability of natural language-based design discussion mining techniques and applies it to compare four content-based mining methods for fundamental design concepts.  

Our findings suggest that the content of a statement plays a crucial role in the stability of design discussion mining, with the initial levels of content aggregation needed to achieve acceptable stability being relatively low.  Notably, our results also highlight substantial variability among different methods for extracting meaningful content from designer conversations.  

Our study underscores the importance of a comprehensive, multi-faceted evaluation approach for design discussion mining methods.

This paper presents H-STREAM, a data management system designed to facilitate big data analysis. It combines real-time data streams and historical datasets into a unified data warehouse for seamless access to both live and past data flows at any given time. To support rapid live data query responses and efficient online query processing, H-STREAM employs a two-tier architecture with a stream engine for real-time query response and a batch data manager for offloaded heavy query processing tasks. Our evaluation demonstrates that this approach outperforms existing stream data management systems and traditional big data querying systems by delivering nearly real-time query responses while delivering nearly twice the query processing speed.

The theoretical model of Topcolor-assisted Dynamism proposes a Topness-deficit problem where the fundamental particles, known as Walker-Topquarks, need to be considered. These particles, proposed to resolve issues with the Topness-deficit problem, can be probed by QCD processes such as Drell-Yan and Fusion. In order to investigate their properties which are dominated by non-resonant diagrams at low-mass region, researchers have employed Monte-Carlo event generator with fixed order cross section and decay analysis. In particular, researchers have analyzed the single production of heavy top and bottom partners at the LHC through both gluon gluon fusion and quark antiquark annihilation processes.

Achieving state-of-the-art results in translating from Romanian to English using SPARQL labels requires an efficient way to cope with substantial knowledge base entries, which traditional neural machine translation models fail to address. This study introduces a straightforward and versatile copy mechanism, tailored for handling knowledge base elements, to the existing SPARQL-NMT model. Incorporating the modified self-attention mechanism allows the enhanced model, called SPARQL-NMT+CM, to outperform the existing model by at least 1.1 points in terms of BLEU score. The accompanying code and data can be accessed at the specified link.

As bibliometric metrics become increasingly influential in academic decision-making, researchers depend on these metrics to evaluate the impact of their work for promotion and funding, often under pressure to demonstrate exceptional research capabilities to academic leaders. To address this challenge, our team has developed a low-cost data analysis tool utilizing venue-specific information, such as conferences and journals, to assign a quantifiable score to individual papers based on their publication venue's characteristics. Our method excels in simplicity and efficiency compared to other bibliometric metrics, such as citation counts and database-assigned scores, and performs comparably to these metrics while also accounting for emerging research trends due to its consideration of co-speakers. Our score demonstrates strong empirical correlation with various established metrics and human evaluations of paper quality.

Advanced learning methods have shown significant potential in addressing complex control issues. Nonetheless, the application of model predictive control (MPC) with neural network approximations has proven challenging. MPC with the aid of these networks can address a broader range of control problems but the method's reliability is limited due to the unpredictable nature of NNs. To address this issue, researchers have developed methods for verifying the correctness of these algorithms. This paper presents a novel neural network verification method, designed to work in conjunction MPC, allowing for the confirmation that certain safety criteria are satisfied. It involves formulating the problem as a sum of squares program to determine the coefficients of a neural network's input based on its parameters, thereby validating its correctness. The proposed method is demonstrated using a simple neural network structure and its computational efficiency is assessed through numerical experiments. The presented framework's correctness and efficiency are further illustrated through a practical example involving motor control.

This study examines how data can be represented as overlapping groups, focusing on developing a clustering approach using this structure. Given a symmetric function measuring the similarity between parts of the data, we aim to identify the most optimal grouping that maximizes overall similarity. Theoretical results confirm the effectiveness of our dynamic programming method in finding the best possible solution in a reasonable computational time. The significance of considering overlapping groupings is demonstrated using both artificial and real-world datasets, highlighting the improved performance and insights compared to traditional, non-overlapping methods.

Tensor completion techniques aim to recover incomplete data in cubic tensors. However, these algorithms traditionally rely on a global approach, using tensor regularization without considering spatial locality in data. This ultimately restricts their ability to recover complete data in large datasets. To address this limitation, a new method called PSTRC has been developed. PSTRC divides tensor data into smaller patches, tracking them across layers to leverage spatial coherence and leverage the tensor regularization of each patch individually. By combining efficient tracking algorithms and parallel processing capabilities, PSTRC achieves better completion performance than completing the entire tensor at once. Furthermore, PSTRC employs an ordered tracking strategy to accelerate convergence and improve coding efficiency using tensor tracking matrices. The method's ability to process and encode patch information separately also makes it well-suited for streaming data. Experiments conducted under various data missing rates demonstrate that PSTRC achieves superior performance in tensor completion tasks.

It is demonstrated that except in three specific instances, the conjugacy classes of classical Weyl groups $W(B_{n})$ and $W(D_{n})$ take the form of type D. This finding has implications for the Nichols algebras associated with irreducible Yetter-Drinfeld modules over the classical Weyl groups $W(B_{n})$ and $W(D_{n})$. Specifically, the order of the Nichols algebras is determined, which serves as a constraint for the classification efforts presented in a complementary publication.

Three-dimensional rotating turbulence, once thought to be dominated by stable geostrophic vortices, has recently been revealed to support vibrant, dynamic wave phenomena. Our study confirms predictions by Gaunard and Thubauze, who found a clear display of anisotropic inertial wave turbulence and a specific energy spectrum with a precise gradient of n/3.

We investigate the maximum weight independent set problem on specific types of graphs, such as those where no two cycles share a single vertex. First, we demonstrate that for these graphs, any maximum weight independent set can be found by normalizing the graph's vertices and then applying a maximum weight independent set algorithm to the resulting graph. Next, we provide an example where normalizing the graph's vertices fails to yield a solution for graphs where all cycles have at least four vertices, showing that this operation can introduce new cycles and alter the graph's structure in a way that prevents finding a maximum weight independent set.

This research study examines the impact of a magnetic field on monolayer graphene's specific heat, Seebeck coefficient, and Tc, when an electric field is applied in-plane. In monolayer graphene, the Dirac fermions can be effectively modeled as a massless gas using the Weyl equation. We calculated the thermodynamic properties and identified a connection between the specific heat and the square of the Seebeck coefficient, showing their combined relationship follows a modified Mott relation. Furthermore, we found that a perpendicularly oriented magnetic field increases the specific heat and Seebeck coefficient at finite doping levels, but these properties decrease in the presence of an in-plane electric field.

Recent findings from Kuznetsov et al. (2021) have identified a low-frequency radio source associated with the binary star system CR Draconis in the 8-13 MHz band. Observations of the system by Kuznetsov et al. revealed radio emission occurring in both an eccentric K-dwarf star (CR Dra A) and its M3.5d dwarf companion (CR Dra B). Following these discoveries, we monitored the system at 7.2 MHz for nearly two years, observing radio emission primarily from the companion star (ECM Dra A) in 7 out of 8 successful sessions. Unusual patterns of radio emission were observed, including variations in peak frequency, signal intensity, and shape, which could not be attributed to the ionosphere. Our study of the radio emission from CR Dra A revealed that its brightness temperature is extremely high, exceeding 10^15 K, and its characteristics suggest the emission mechanism is electron-cyclotron maser activity generated by the star's magnetic field. Our analysis suggests that low-latitude stellar fields could be responsible for the observed radio emission, and future studies in a near-infrared band could provide insights into the star's non-thermal activity.

By combining traditional rendering techniques with neural networks, Deferred
Neural Renderer (DNR) achieved a new milestone in virtual human avatars.
Achieving photorealistic results, DNR required significant computational power,
and failed to account for dynamic interactions between skin and underlying muscle
movement. This research proposes a novel approach, ANR, to generate interactive
avatars in real-time using pre-generated images. ANR employs a computationally
efficient, surface-based shading method to simulate accurate shadow and contact
point interactions, and integrates skin subsurface scattering, or SSS, to enhance
realism. For effective global illumination, DNR is utilized, and our method has been
evaluated using multiple avatars, achieving high-quality visual results with
lower computational requirements.

Recent advances in artificial intelligence, including generative models, enable the creation of altered images that can be shown to humans for testing. A crucial factor in this area is the effect of such transformations on recognition systems that can be easily evaluated, yet human responses to these changes remain less understood. An empirical study was conducted to examine how extreme color and distortion transformations impact both human and machine image classification, revealing that distorted transformations significantly affect human performance. Furthermore, this study found that different approaches to artificial transformations, including GANs, do not produce the same results as simple distortion methods, and that human and machine perception differences persist across various tasks.

The Askey-Wilson algebra was found to be relevant in describing the link invariants associated with certain two-color links within the theory of Chern-Simons, particularly when the gauge group is either $SU(2)$ or $U(2)$. It was demonstrated that, in this context, the Askey-Wilson algebra acts on the color spaces defined by Wilson loop operators and the link invariants can be computed using universal central elements of the algebra's quotient, which results in rational expressions based on quantum integers.

Our study uses the cluster quantum Monte Carlo method to investigate the magnetic properties of frustrated trimer lattices with weak couplings, covering both tetrameric and percolating trimer lattices with various boundary conditions. We analyze the trimer's response to an external magnetic field as well as its intrinsic spin dynamics, which are characterized through the intrinsic frequency $\omega_{in}$. Furthermore, we investigate the formation of magnetic holons bound to the trimer corners due to the trivacancy trimer defect's presence. Observables such as the structure factor, trimer flux, and intrinsic frequency are analyzed in relation to the intratrimer coupling strength to identify the Haldane gap phase transition. Trimer flux analysis reveals evidence for the transition between the Haldane gap and the spin liquid phase at low intratrimer coupling values in both models, with the percolating trimer model exhibiting an additional transition at very low intratrimer coupling values, where it enters a trivacancy polarized phase. Spin dynamics within the Haldane gap phase are accurately described by the percolating trimer model, where they are characterized by an energy gap that increases as the intratrimer coupling value decreases. Additionally, we find that the percolating trimer model provides a reliable approximation for the Hamiltonian description of certain materials in the Ag$_2$Mn$_3$O$_6$ family.

Recent advancements in pre-trained language models (PLMs) utilizing the Transformer architecture have been highly beneficial for natural language processing (NLP) tasks. Recent research has explored using PLMs for zero-shot learning across NLP, but significant performance disparities persist among various datasets. To address this discrepancy, two novel methods have been proposed: PLM method involves adapting PLMs through a meta-learning approach on NLP task collections, whereas the Prompt set method focuses on assembling a set of prompts rather than adapting the PLMs. Both approaches yield substantial improvements in accuracy and have shown promise in handling previously unseen tasks.

In this investigation, the researchers focus on the potential of the $Z_3$-invariant NMSSM to achieve a strong first-order electroweak phase transition, resulting in detectable gravitational waves by LISA. The study, incorporating recent findings from the LHC and dark matter searches, reveals that the model's parameter space for generating gravitational waves of interest is significantly restricted, with the dark matter candidate being a LSP near the upper bound of the Higgsino mass. This near-degeneracy of LSP masses leads to considerable improvements in the indirect detection of gravitational waves via neutral pair production at the LHC and a reduced neutrino flux from annihilation, bringing the model into agreement with the current bounds on indirect detection. The model's implications for the Higgs sector are also explored in the study through calculations of its tree-level and loop-corrected properties.

We introduce novel techniques for visually and automatically assessing the reliability of (sub)mm spectroscopic redshifts using Sudoku-like diagrams. The proposed classification system ranges from high robustness (High-z Sudoku type A/B/C) to low robustness (High-z Sudoku type D/E/F). When applied to the SOFIA FUSE sample at z~0.3 and the ALFAMA dataset at z~0.5, the manual classification showed strong correlation with previously established robust-spectrum criteria. Furthermore, we developed a machine learning model that utilizes spectral data to predict High-z Sudoku types, with several types being more reliable than established standards for selecting robust spectra. The ML classifier's predictions demonstrate substantial overlap with previously successful redshift determination methods.

In the $S=1/2$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic lattice with a triangular structure, a specific feature known as a "butterfly pattern" emerges at the dynamical level, corresponding to the spin liquid phase at low energies. Notably, this butterfly pattern shares similarities with the dynamical behavior exhibited by a regime at high magnetic fields and a order phase known as the 120-degree ordering. While a finite temperature may cause some features to diminish, the spin liquid phase's low-energy "butterfly pattern" remains distinct and noticeable, particularly in conditions of low temperatures.

The study investigates lattice confinement-deconfinement transitions in $SU(3)-$Higgs theories using the Bruckner-Wegner-Polyakov order parameter under various boundary conditions. Numerational results obtained from Monte Carlo simulations at different gauging strengths, initial volumes, and initial Higgs field values reveal a specific pattern of phase transitions. For the periodic boundaries case, the system exhibits a re-confinement transition when the coupling constant is decreased from the deconfined phase, with the critical Higgs coupling value increasing as the system size decreases and then decreasing once the finite size effect becomes noticeable. On the other hand, for the torus boundaries case, the system transitions from the deconfined phase to the confined phase as the coupling constant is lowered, with the critical Higgs coupling value increasing as the coupling value is lowered and then decreasing once it passes a turning point.

Cr$_2$Al exhibits a re-entrant antiferromagnetic phase that emerges at
50 K following a initial phase transition at 60 K. This study presents a
detailed examination of its magnetic properties across a broad temperature and
magnetic field range, including the in-plane magnetic structure. Neutron
diffraction findings show that Cr$_2$Al follows an easy-axis type g-vector
with a out-of-plane magnetic structure and an easy-axis along the c-axis. In
addition, it is discovered that a small spontaneous Cr moment exists in this
material. As expected, applying a magnetic field causes the sample to transition
into a paramagnetic state, and a measurement of the sample's magnetization
revealed a clear dependence on its magnetic field orientation. In contrast to
other Cr$_2$X compounds, where Cr moments lie perpendicular to their axis,
this study establishes that Cr$_2$Al possesses exchange interactions that
follow a specific two-subsystem model. This finding is further confirmed by
first-principles calculations.

A new kinetic model is developed for rarefied monatomic gas flows near the transition flow regime, incorporating collision frequency that varies with flow velocity and flow angular collision numbers. These are derived from generalized Boltzmann's equation for specific intermolecular potentials such as the hard sphere, soft sphere, and variable speed of sound models. Numerical simulations using a lattice Boltzmann method show that this new model accurately predicts flow behavior for specific angular collision numbers and flow regimes. It captures how the intermolecular potential influences flow behavior, as evidenced through comparisons with simulations using different potentials and numerical calculations. Notably, the new model performs well for angular collision numbers below 10, yielding collision frequencies that vary significantly, unlike kinetic models based on kinetic theory which assume constant collision frequencies and show larger deviations from expected results in this range.

Semantic parsers translate natural language input into logical forms, but typically depend on being trained using data generated based on specific rules. This report examines how data conversion techniques can help make trained parsers more applicable to unseen data without requiring additional training. Several conversion methods are compared, and the results show that no singular method works best across all cases, underscoring the importance of using a diverse set of training data that closely resembles live data in the first place.

The Electron-Ion Collider's future will involve utilizing electron-proton and electron-nucleus collisions to thoroughly investigate the fundamental components of matter. To effectively determine crucial data, precise measurement methods are necessary, particularly in identifying faint hadrons that prove to be a substantial challenge. To address this, cutting-edge technologies for forward proton and neutron detection, alongside hadron identification, are being developed and will be discussed.

A new finding in a low-mass AGN called NGC 4103 has been made by the ZTF, 
revealing a significant change in its brightness of about 0.4 magnitudes over a 
short period. The change occurred in the visual spectrum and was detected in 
2021. The change in brightness shares similarities with another type of variability 
that occurs over a shorter timescale, but the recent change is more intense and 
occurs in the visual spectrum. Researchers are still trying to understand the exact 
cause of this change, but possible explanations include instability caused by 
accretion, disk oscillations or small disk eruptions. By studying the change in 
brightness, researchers can gain a better understanding of how low-mass AGNs work 
and how they evolve. The recent change in brightness is the first in its kind 
that has been found in a low-mass AGN, but future research is needed to confirm 
its exact cause and to understand how this phenomenon affects other low-mass AGNs.

Recent research suggests that magnetic fields in the convection zones of cool stars can be amplified by a dynamo process, leading to increased spot formation. The high-activity star HD58260, however, challenges this idea, as it exhibits stable, strong global magnetic fields without significant spot patterns. A hypothesis proposes that these fields are amplified by unusual mechanisms. Our analysis of HD58260's magnetic fields reveals that they are concentrated at the star's equator and extend into its atmosphere, indicating a significant radial gradient. The equatorial fields are stronger and more prevalent, contrasting with the magnetic fields at the star's poles, where they approach near zero. The radial gradient in HD58260's magnetic fields exceeds its surface gradient, implying the presence of strong fields within chromospheric emission lines. The equatorial regions exhibit a greater abundance of dipoles compared to quadrupoles, contrasting with the global fields, and suggesting that magnetohydrodynamic instabilities may contribute to field amplification.

A link exists between a Dunkl operator over a field with two elements and a first derivative, 
exemplified through its equivalence to an operator comprising a derivative and a trigonometric function 
within a one-dimensional framework, which constitutes a simpler manifestation of this relationship. 
Notably, the corresponding kernel of the associated Dunkl operator mirrors the well-established connection 
between a Laplacian and a free boson field, when viewed in a suitably transformed form.

A recent discovery has shown that high-density gas in the quiescent regions of galaxies primarily contributes to star formation. The SFR metric developed by Schinnerer et al. (2020) leverages this notion by integrating the emission from the gas molecules' fine structure. However, the SFR metric has been tested using Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) data collected at a shorter wavelength of 3.6 mm, which could be contaminated by cooler gas that doesn't participate in star formation. The current study re-evaluates the effectiveness of the SFR metric by comparing it to the conventional SFR metric, which is based on CO data observed by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at 870 GHz. The analysis focuses on the galaxy NGC 5253, which has been observed by the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) at both 3.6 mm and 870 GHz. The observations indicate that the SFR metric observed at 3.6 mm and 870 GHz are closely correlated, which suggests that the Schinnerer et al. (2020) SFR metric is not significantly affected by the presence of cooler gas. The research also reveals that the SFR metric observed at 3.6 mm is less variable and has a lower detection threshold, which makes it a valuable tool for studying

We demonstrate that two continuous minimal actions of the infinite dihedral group on an infinite compact Hausdorff space can be orbit equivalent if and only if they are conjugate, provided the group acting on the space has an infinite compact open subgroup.

We introduce a novel, data-driven framework for approximating an infinite-dimensional operator $T$ in a Hilbert space by a finite-dimensional operator in the same space. The proposed method does not rely on any assumptions about the structure of $T$ and utilizes empirical data to determine the optimal parameters for the approximating operator. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the accuracy of the proposed approach, dividing the error into a bias and variance component. The resulting error bound yields insights into selecting the optimal approximating model that minimizes estimation error and implies the existence of such a model. We conduct a simulation study evaluating the performance of our approach across various types of data and operator classes. Additionally, we apply our method to estimate the conditional probability density of stratum-specific net benefit given a given dose of radiation from simulated and actual datasets.

Designing effective state observers for nonlinear epidemic models is crucial for analyzing and controlling their behavior. This study focuses on developing state observers for the SIR and SIRI models to support decision-making in epidemiology. For the given models, we establish existence and convergence conditions for observers within the context of the Euclidean space R3, assuming we can measure the total number of susceptible and infected individuals. These conditions are derived based on a local approach, utilizing local observability and Lipschitz continuity of the model vector field. We further propose a novel, linear observer and compare its performance with that of a non-linear quadratic program-based observer. These proposed observers are applied in decision support for optimal policy analysis using computational simulations.

The growing importance of large temporal knowledge graphs has led to the development of various studies focusing on representing these representations and addressing problems such as completion of incomplete information. Nevertheless, previous approaches often neglect proposed static models for representing knowledge graph information. This research aims to develop a new approach for temporal knowledge graph representation and completion of missing information. We have created a new unsupervised method for imputing temporal knowledge graph information using the static model as a reference. This method involves a new hybrid approach for completing missing information that combines the insights from both static and temporal representations. We have extensively evaluated our proposed method using synthetic and real-world datasets, showing superior performance compared to other comparison methods. We provide our code for publicly accessible review at https://github.com/alexandroskats/mytpe.

Research driven by ultrashort pulses from Kerr-lens mode-locked oscillators has expanded rapidly, thanks to advancements in theory and technology. As peak power increases however, Kerr-lens mode-locking becomes more complex, requiring deeper analysis. This has led to the development of fundamental equations describing the crucial cavity mirror confocal parameter in terms of key design elements such as cavity length, gain bandwidth, beam waist, loss, and pulse duration. These equations are essential for understanding the transformation from continuous wave to Kerr-lens mode-locking and the eventual Q-switched pulse collapse. They are applicable to a wide range of setups including ring resonators, linear cavities with both real and virtual beams, and provide a valuable design tool for Kerr-lens mode-locked oscillators.

Online learning methods have been widely applied to handle massive datasets with limited computational resources. However, for tasks like nonlinear regression, online learning methods have not received sufficient attention. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a novel asynchronous federated learning framework designed for resource-constrained settings, where a device learns a model from its local data without sharing it with others. The model updates are performed using stochastic gradient descent, taking into account non-convex, non-differentiable loss functions through subgradient descent. This framework allows for model training on streaming or partial datasets, and can be utilized in various applications such as time series forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that this framework converges faster and more efficiently than synchronous SGD, especially when dealing with constrained devices, while also outperforming other methods in terms of efficiency.

To improve the efficiency of thin-film silicon solar cells by increasing absorption of light, an anti-reflection coating and a 3D back reflector are suggested. Specifically, employing a back reflector made of a 3D woodpile photonic crystal in silicon can effectively reduce light transmission through the thin films. The characteristics of these photonic crystals can be tuned based on their air sphere radius, spacing between spheres, and the thickness of silicon, thereby improving absorption of light across various thin films. For very thin absorber layers, an ultrathin film of silicon can be highly efficient in absorbing light by incorporating a thin film of approximately 200 nanometers in thickness and an lattice constant of 500 nanometers for the photonic crystal back reflector.

We explore tetration for both complex and real bases, and prove that as the iteration count approaches infinity, the magnitude of this value also approaches infinity, regardless of initial conditions and a few singular exceptions. We introduce and analyze infinite power towers for bases within the annulus $e^{-e} \leq |b| \leq e$, and the infinite power tower is well-defined outside the measure-zero set consisting of critical points and singularities. Our findings include the proof that for bases within the disk $|b| \leq e^{1/3}$, the iterations converge to specific limits: a periodic orbit of length six in the case where $b$ is a 6th root of $e$, and absolute convergence to 1 in the case where $b$ is the 21st root of $e$. Additionally, we examine the asymptotic behavior of tetration for bases outside the disk $|b| \leq 2e^{1/3}$, and derive the following conclusions: as the iteration count approaches infinity, the magnitude of tetration for bases within the annulus $2 \leq |b| \leq e^{e}$ approaches infinity; more specifically, for bases within the annulus $2+\epsilon \leq |b| \leq e^{e}$, the real part of the $z$-th tetration approaches $z \log_b e$, and the imaginary part approaches a periodic function with a

We've developed a novel method for creating high dimensional expanders, potentially yielding faster and more efficient algorithms. This involves utilizing group theory techniques, specifically non-ambient covers of simplicial complexes. In particular, we leverage the symmetry inherent in the Leech lattice to generate exceptional high dimensional expanders.

Researchers discovered the existence of the magnetic compound GdInO3 with a centered honeycomb structure through both theoretical prediction and experimental analysis. The compound was synthesized by solid-state reaction and undergoes a hexagonal crystalline transition at 1260 K, exhibiting antiferromagnetic properties with a Néel temperature (TN) of approximately 1.11 K. Magnetic measurements indicate two distinct phases when the compound is cooled in a direct current (dc) field, including a linear magnetization in the low-field range and magnetic saturation at around 0.15 Gd3+ muB per unit cell at high fields. Based on an Heisenberg spin-Hamiltonian, the compound was found to have two primary exchange interactions, where the distance between adjacent sites and those six units apart have specific coupling constants (J1 and J5) and others are negligible. The ground state magnetic structure is characterized by two-fold and three-fold folding of the Brillouin zone due to these interactions. The study further suggests the possibility of a Haldane gap or a spin liquid state due to the geometric frustration inherent in the compound.

The task of link prediction, which aims to identify potential connections between nodes, has significant applications in various fields.  Despite the benefits, large-scale networks often suffer from sparse structural information.  In this paper, we introduce SSNE, a link prediction method designed specifically for sparse networks.  Our approach utilizes a network compression technique based on spectral clustering, which enables link reconstruction even in networks with limited information.  To assess the effectiveness of SSNE, we apply it to three major social networks.  To our knowledge, this is the first study to employ spectrum-based node representation for link prediction, and our results demonstrate that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

A low-cost water-based deep silicon etching process has been developed to manufacture thin-film atomic vapor cells with high optical depth. The process produces a high yield of high-quality micro-fabricated silicon cells that are transparent to light, as demonstrated by the uniform transmission of 532 nm light through cells 350 micrometers to 80 micrometers thick. The new cell design outperforms other cell types by achieving an energy storage capacity comparable to that of thicker glass-silicon boron alloy cells, thanks to its unique material and geometric properties. The new technology also eliminates the need for noble gases in the cells, as performance tests on room temperature skin deep etched by the process show a signal that increases linearly with the thickness of the silicon layer and does not show the characteristic non-linear saturation typically seen in thicker silicon cells or when doped silicon is used as the wall material.

We evaluate the precision of a recently proposed nonlinear interference model for a wide range of dual-polarization fourth-order complex formats. The enhanced model, which incorporates the spectral width of a format as well as its root mean square (RMS) symbol power, symbol kurtosis, and normalized fourth-order spectral cross-correlation coefficient, shows improved accuracy, achieving less than 0.5 dB relative root mean square error (RMS) when compared to fourth-order complex formats, as opposed to the traditional four-symbol model developed byNZ.

Wildfires significantly impact ecosystems, human lives, and property, causing extensive damage and destruction. Effective fire management relies heavily on timely detection and situational awareness, which can be greatly enhanced through the use of fused visible and infrared images. These fused images provide more comprehensive spatial, spectral, and temporal insights to support decision-making in fire management. In this research, a Deep Learning-based fusion model, FIRe-GAN, is introduced to produce high-quality fused images directly by matching statistical properties between synthetic and real fused images. The model achieved superior performance compared to existing techniques in multiple fusion metrics and provided the most suitable output for wildfire monitoring. Additionally, a pre-trained model was successfully applied in real-world scenarios and shared publicly to facilitate further research and development.

Early detection and treatment of depression can prevent severe outcomes,
such as suicide. By leveraging social media analysis, it's possible to identify
early indicators of depression through a technique called digital phenotyping.
A key challenge is developing effective machine learning models for detecting
depression signs on social media. Our study introduces a new social media data
set featuring a time-series structure from individuals diagnosed with depression
and those without mental health issues. We employed the natural language
processing tool, SpaCy, to fine-tune classifiers capable of identifying
progressive language patterns indicative of depression using multiple language
models. Our analysis revealed certain pre-crisis language characteristics
associated with a heightened risk of suicidal behavior. Our code and data are
open-source at https://github.com/abhishekdabre/Depression_Detection.

We present a stochastic cohort model that captures the dynamics of a COVID-19 epidemic within a closed population, which is grounded in within-generation deterministic equations previously established by Lachowicz et al. (2021). The model's discrete-time stochastic version maintains the same states as its continuous deterministic counterpart, however, we explore an alternative formulation ensuring all simulated states adhere to the constraints imposed by the model's parameters. The model's solution constitutes a Markov chain defined on non-negative rational numbers, and its domain is confined by parameter-specific bounds. We validate the model through extensive numerical simulations and assess its utility through a case study involving the COVID-19 epidemic in Rio de Janeiro.

Using the Shell Model, we've conducted a thorough investigation into the isoscalar giant monopole resonance (MGMR) in $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si. Our research reveals that the MGMR in these two isotopes is significantly influenced by its coupling with quadrupole strength. This effect results in a notable difference in the isoscalar monopole elastic peak and the isoscalar monopole resonance energy between $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si. In particular, we've found that the experimental ISGMR energy in $^{24}$Mg is 20.75$\pm$0.18 MeV, whereas it is 21.08$\pm$0.14 MeV in $^{28}$Si. Our study also demonstrates that the coupling between MGMR and quadrupole strength can lead to a substantial shift in the ISGMR energy between $^{24}$Mg and $^{28}$Si, and emphasizes the necessity of considering configuration interactions within the calculation of the ISGMR in the shell model. Our research further illustrates the importance of taking into account low-lying states in the wave function to obtain a more precise description of the ISGMR in finite nuclei.

A study on stick-slip dynamics and the convergence of motion paths in systems governed by Coulomb friction is conducted. The existence of a universally attractive funnel, through which all trajectories converge, along with its geometric properties, has been theoretically demonstrated. These findings offer crucial insights into the development of robust controllers for friction-affected systems. The theoretical framework developed is then applied to two practical scenarios: first, to show that the motion of a block under Coulomb friction always reaches a stable state regardless of initial conditions or friction coefficients; second, to examine the convergence properties and achieve performance targets in a universal joint system subject to Coulomb friction and driven through proportional control.

A novel reinforcement learning method based on the actor-critic architecture specifically targets the task of minimizing financial risk over extended periods through the implementation of an innovative learned compensator learning algorithm. This approach effectively learns to match target risk characteristics by targeting the risk-sensitive criterion directly, requiring no task-specific tuning beyond the initial criterion setting, offering enhanced model-agnostic flexibility. This technique is demonstrated on both simulated and real-world robotic manipulation tasks including diverse grid-world simulations, as well as 7-DOF and 8-DOF robotic applications utilizing 400 and 1000 high-frequency LiDAR sensors respectively, successfully validating its capacity to both learn risk-correcting actions where failure incloses catastrophic consequences, as well as apply this method to risk correction across diverse domains.

In today's recommendation systems, the most advanced models are capable of handling complex tasks by considering sequential user behaviors and item contexts. However, there's room for improvement as these models typically fall short in accurately modeling users' underlying goals. We propose an innovative approach that leverages the power of transformers to create a discrete latent variable space representing user goals, making it possible to train the model end-to-end through a novel two-stage training technique that combines online and target distribution methods. We demonstrate through comprehensive testing across various real-world datasets that this approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art recomender models in terms of prediction accuracy and user goal representation quality.

It also marks a significant difference when applied to other forms of the Heun equation.
