Achieving high performance in multilingual machine learning is resource-intensive, 
as models requiring large amounts of memory and processing power are impractical for deployment.
This study explores two approaches, knowledge distillation and quantization, to reduce the resource demands 
of state-of-the-art multilingual models, focusing on their relative stability and effectiveness in achieving 
lightweight models with low resource specifications, such as 2 bytes or 4. We applied these methods to 
various language pairs for translation tasks, including evaluating weighted word error rates, model parameters, 
and the FLOPs of the resulting models. Our findings reveal that while distillation often results in better 
performance, it fails to significantly reduce model sizes below the original teacher model's size.
Quantization, though less effective in enhancing performance, successfully compresses models, surpassing the 
resource demands of its teacher model's requirements. Moreover, we highlight the challenges associated with 
quantization's convergence when moving from lower to lower precision, underscoring its inherent instability.
This research contributes a comprehensive understanding of the multilingual setting's implications for both 
quantization and distillation, as well as their respective limitations.

The edge graph of an hypergraph G, constructed such that it contains a projective plane graph, exhibits a Lagrangian density of the natural number 3 when viewed as a projective plane graph, however, as an hypergraph, it demonstrates a non-rational Lagrangian density, providing a counterexample to the hypothesis that Lagrangian densities of all hypergraphs with a simple structure are rational numbers.

The detection and identification of chest X-ray abnormalities, such as those caused by pneumonia, can be achieved through the techniques of image segmentation and classification. Recent advancements in deep learning have led to improved performance in these tasks, but such models rely heavily on extensive datasets with high annotation costs. To overcome this challenge, a novel strategy is introduced that utilizes unperturbed images to produce unperturbed images as well as various perturbed versions, which are subsequently applied to a segment any shape network to enhance its ability to generalize. To evaluate this method's effectiveness, we conducted experiments on two networks using the MONI2M-Net dataset. These experiments demonstrated that our proposed approach using unperturbed images as a means of data augmentation can significantly enhance the accuracy of segmentation and classification tasks. Furthermore, we found that by employing asymptotically optimal change of variable techniques, our ASNet approach was able to reduce the labelled data requirement for accurate segmentation by 20-30%.

Image captioning generates text descriptions that align with people's perceptions
of a scene's content and context. Although this functionality is largely
accomplished by existing image captioning models, they typically struggle to
produce context-dependent text. This paper presents a new image captioning model
utilizing prompt learning to enhance its flexibility and adaptability. The model
excels in generating diverse, detailed, and accurate captions, excelling in
multiple benchmark tests. By integrating in-text and out-of-text optimization,
the proposed method achieves superior image caption quality. Furthermore,
this paper explores the mechanisms behind the model's performance.

As autonomous systems become increasingly prevalent, it is essential to establish a legal and ethical framework for assessing harm, particularly in the context of harm caused by autonomous systems. This study contributes a causal theory of harm suitable for application in various scenarios, drawing on recent research regarding causation. It is demonstrated that established principles of causation lead to conclusions about harm that resonate with pre-existing harm theories. Furthermore, autonomous system-specific concerns are addressed, and proposed solutions are discussed.

This study showcases MMLSpark, an innovative open-source library that bridges the gap between PyTorch and Spark AI, enabling a more Spark-centric and collaborative training approach for deep learning models. The emphasis is placed on developing depth-wise convolutional neural networks (CNNs) in collaboration with Spark for image processing tasks like classification and segmentation. The proposed solution addresses key limitations of existing frameworks, which are more focused on application-wise convolutions, by incorporating data-parallelism and improving the scalability of image processing. The deep study reveals how data-parallel processing impacts training and the extent to which MMLSpark meets the need for efficient flexibility. The proposed method also explores the trade-offs of live versus batch processing approaches and highlights the benefits of leveraging GPU accelerators. The paper presents a more comprehensive understanding of training with data-parallel processing and demonstrates the effectiveness of leveraging GPU accelerators. The proposed solution showcases efficient scaling on real-world datasets and demonstrates the benefits of modular design and flexibility in training with large-scale data.

Speech-to-text translation directly converts spoken language from a source language to a target language without requiring reconstructed text, focusing on zero-shot conditions, where translation capabilities arise from merely exposure to speech and text samples in both the source and target languages. Achieving this goal presents unique challenges to existing neural approaches as they were primarily designed with pre-existing translation knowledge. Our study demonstrates a method of extracting speech-to-text pairs through self-supervised learning using pseudo-alignment models, allowing knowledge transfer from existing audio-to-text and speech-to-text models to reinforce newly derived pairs. Additionally, a novel transformation is introduced to incorporate prior translation knowledge into self-supervised models, resulting in significantly enhanced performance in speech-to-text translation without requiring additional model tuning.

This work introduces a novel extension of the traditional heat conduction theory, encompassing cases with fading memory and incorporating the standard heat equation under dynamic boundary conditions as a special instance. The study delves into the well-posedness of systems comprised of equations akin to those by Coleman and Gurtin, further supplemented with Neumann-type conditions on the boundary and intra-boundary. Initially, it establishes a proof of existence and uniqueness for linear systems with given data, followed by an examination of the behavior of non-linear counterparts in relation to their linear counterparts, ultimately yielding a demonstration of existence and uniqueness for non-linear systems under dynamic boundary conditions.

Precise forecasting of future electricity consumption is crucial for managing low voltage networks efficiently, minimizing peak loads, and reducing transfer capacities. To this end, we developed an innovative approach that combines forecasts from multiple models with peak identification techniques. The integrated framework not only achieves accurate overall energy predictions but also accurately captures most daily peak energy usages within the forecasting horizon. The effectiveness of this new approach was confirmed through testing under real-world conditions.

The growth of machine learning algorithms has not kept pace with the increasing demand for fully automated data science processes. Currently, the need to manually annotate data to ensure accurate predictions places a significant burden on available resources. As a result, researchers are actively seeking alternative strategies that can minimize costs, and a promising approach involves the incorporation of domain knowledge in machine learning models to facilitate their operation. A substantial body of literature highlights the effectiveness of domain knowledge integration in various machine learning tasks, yet many of these studies lack visibility and their contributions remain underappreciated. In an effort to rectify this, this paper provides a comprehensive overview of methods for integrating domain knowledge in machine learning models. It begins by outlining the different forms domain knowledge can take, and then examines the various methods for facilitating knowledge flow between domain experts and machine learning algorithms. A notable challenge lies in the absence of a unified framework for evaluating the performance of domain knowledge integration methods, and therefore, this paper proposes a roadmap for conducting systematic evaluations. It further presents case studies illustrating how domain knowledge integration can enhance the performance of machine learning models, and concludes by discussing current limitations and potential areas for future research.

Creating a reliable model for precise COVID-19 detection on chest CT scans poses significant difficulties due to limited annotated data, biases, and varying quality of training sets. To overcome these challenges, we utilize a step-wise approach that employs image-level labels, leveraging well-known transfer learning methods, and an advanced pixel-level change segmentation technique inspired by unbiased change segmentation methods. Furthermore, we propose an innovative weakly supervised pixel-level change detection method, leveraging image-level labels, that develops models both without and with pseudo-ground truth data to prevent bias during pixel-level detection and segmentation. These novel approaches demonstrate superior performance on multiple publicly available COVID-19 chest CT scan datasets, showcasing their effectiveness and accuracy.

This research introduces an advanced, fully automated method for identifying and marking vertebrae in spine CT scans. The proposed technique, built on a method previously published, involves aligning vertebrae in a frontal plane and then utilizes a precise modeling approach to determine the boundaries of each vertebrae in the spine. Conventional methods often rely on complex and time-consuming manual checks or error-prone deep learning algorithms. Our method surpasses these limitations by requiring minimal user interaction and guaranteeing accurate results. Several experiments were conducted to verify the efficacy of the proposed method, and the results show that our approach successfully locates and marks vertebrae in a diverse range of complex spinal conditions, including scoliosis, with impressive precision. Notably, our approach demonstrates high performance in the most challenging cases, where vertebrae overlap or are misaligned. Our research demonstrates the potential of a highly efficient and accurate method for vertebrae detection and marking in complex spine CT scans.

Our study investigates the resonance scattering of an electron by a two-level molecule strongly coupled to an ultrafast electron microscope beam, which is exposed to quantized electromagnetic fields within a cavity. Even when far from the typical conditions for strong interaction, a broad, dipper-shaped pattern appears in a lower-energy range of the scenario. Conversely, a typical Lorentz-shaped resonance is observed at a higher energy level. Moreover, multiple narrow resonances emerge at high laser energies, which are interpreted as a manifestation of dynamical stabilization, initially predicted approximately 40 years ago. Specifically, the typical light-matter interaction regime is distinguished from regions of strong-light-matter coupling in terms of electron scattering cross-sections. Within the strong-light-matter coupling regime, a typical resonance at low energies is significantly suppressed due to cavity-modified light-matter interactions, whereas all other resonances are diminished by vacuum field back-action on the molecule.

The future of legged robots lies in equipping them with elastic actuators that combine compliance and power, making dynamic movement feasible and increasing safety for interactions with humans and surroundings. The key challenge in developing these hybrid actuated quadrupeds is mastering their complex dynamics. This study presents an innovative approach where a deep reinforcement learning agent controls a soft-body model that simulates the combined mechanical and dynamic properties of a model equipped with elastic actuators featuring series elastic actuators and compliant legs. The learned agent successfully transfers to a physical quadruped that moves effectively at varied speeds and tackles obstacles, demonstrating superior performance over an actuated model without serial elasticity and outperforming an optimal controller with serial elasticity but without foot compliance.

We propose a new approach based on a variational principle for calculating the entropy of entanglement of a pure state within a subsystem of a composite quantum system. By providing an upper limit to this measure, the method can resolve whether mixed quantum states of subsystems are separable, specifically for systems consisting of two subsystems with small dimensions. We apply this method to derive the Binder gap in the 1D transverse field Ising model, showing that it exhibits long-range order at zero temperature that is disrupted by a phase transition triggered by the transverse field.

A well-documented phenomenon in various plasma systems, small-scale magnetic reconnection, often arises due to electron pressure anisotropy in the form of a tearing mode. Through extensive numerical simulations and analytical analysis, this research explores the characteristics of a finite-k wave number in electron-scale plasma regions with finite electron collision rates. Under the specific condition that the electron temperature significantly exceeds the ion temperature, this research shows that small-scale tearing modes exhibit enhanced magnetic spectrum modes and exhibit increased magnetic flux component ratios, despite being weakly unstable. Analytically derived solutions confirm these findings. Numerical and analytical comparisons also reveal significant nonlinear effects on these solutions, which typically play a minor role in traditional plasma regimes but can substantially influence these small-scale tearing modes. Additionally, this research explores the implications of these findings on magnetic reconnection in the Earth's magnetosphere, suggesting a potential instability-driven electron-scale magnetic flux component ratio and the significant role of these small-scale tearing modes in magnetic reconnection processes even at low collision rates.

A surge in interest has accompanied the resurgence of digital fashion. As a result, researchers are now exploring computer vision applications, including fashion image retrieval, which involves matching a query image with similar images representing the same garment. Traditionally, existing methods rely heavily on large datasets annotated with fashion categories and specific fashion attributes, such as color, style, and pattern. Unfortunately, obtaining accurate ground truth datasets is a costly endeavor and limits potential applications to limited domains. To address these challenges, we introduce a pioneering technique that enables the manipulation of attributes from a query image to generate accurate, annotated datasets without requiring pixel-level manipulation. This technique leverages existing fashion datasets, allowing the production of vast amounts of synthesized data, thereby eliminating the need for expensive human annotation. By adopting a feature-level manipulation method, we can bypass the need for costly pixel-level manipulation techniques. Our novel approach demonstrates the effectiveness of this image manipulation technique, yielding results comparable to those achieved using real human-annotated datasets, while outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods in a cost-efficient manner.

The ill-posed problems Tx=y are reconsidered with a focus on its dual problem x*=T' '*y* subject to the constraint ||x*||' '*=1, which has previously been studied by H. Wachsmuth in terms of existence and uniqueness solutions. Our work utilizes the dual gradient flow to tackle this constraint-embedded equation and, assuming the space, T, and φ are convex and smooth respectively, and given an initial condition in the domain of T', we prove the existence and uniqueness of the solution to the constraint-embedded equation. Furthermore, under an additional condition, we show that the support of the solution lies within the pre-image of T' applied to y*.

Constructing the cost function is a critical step in estimating light field depth but
its methods often rely on assumptions such as occlusion invariance, local consistency,
and non-stretchability that are frequently violated in the cost model.
In light field depth estimation, features from boundary areas and non-corresponding
pixels are typically disregarded or treated as valuable information, leading to suboptimal
performance. Our approach presents an innovative concept and a unique architecture, 
OC³CT, designed to efficiently handle cost model violations. OC³CT utilizes a dual-loop
U-Net and a custom decoder to identify and handle occluded regions. It then employs a 
two-stage process: a learning stage to identify boundaries and data points that are not well
illuminated, and a refinement stage to refine features in the occluded areas. Our approach's 
performance surpasses the state-of-the-art in various light field depth estimation scenarios.

This study uses the bilinear method to investigate the Fokas-Lenells equations, a recent development in integrable systems. By employing the generalized Hirota-Darboux transformation, we derive expressions for exact solitons and obtain various solutions such as those with a single peak and interactions between waves with different shapes. Our analysis reveals that the Fokas-Lenells equations are a significant extension of the Chen-Lax equations and the coupled Chen-Lax equations, which are both specialized instances of the former, with the coupled version occurring when specific parameters are set to zero.

Our 10D theory space approach closely mirrors Nieuwenhuyzen and Nutma's 8D method, but we adopt the formalism proposed by Hohm and Tzetradis for the 10D background. We find that an additional kinetic term similar to that used by Nutma is necessary, as a single term from the DDBS is insufficient to describe a non-Riemannian gravitational theory. By applying the standard HSTBS poress procedures, we derive two viable 6D PoH actions. One matches the existing Niu's action, whereas the other represents a previously unknown formulation. We explore the link between our findings and Galois' work on 10D non-Riemannian gravity, noting similarities and differences in our derived actions compared to Galois'  kinetic terms.

In home WiFi networks, multiple access points and extenders often coexist, 
leading to intricate wireless local area networks with uneven distribution of 
access points indoors and outdoors.  As a result, clients may face difficulties 
associating with the most suitable access point.  To address this issue, we 
develop a channel-aware algorithm that determines optimal access points or 
extenders for clients and facilitates smooth handovers through reference 
channel switching.  Our multi-stage verification process, carried out under 
various indoor and outdoor conditions, demonstrates the load-balancing efficacy 
of our channel selection algorithm, which is also ensured by the IEEE 802.11v 
BSS Transition Management protocol.  Notably, we observe that it takes less 
than one second to successfully migrate clients from one access point to another, 
while experiencing a 22.2% improvement in terms of data transfer speed.
